ex: Stress is a common trigger for my headaches.
What is the trigger for your allergy?
Loud noise can be a trigger for my dog.
Try to avoid your asthma triggers, like smoke and dust.
trigger.note: Often the part of a gun you pull: "pull the trigger." As a verb: "Stress can trigger headaches."

symptom.say: a symptom of (the flu) · have symptoms
ex: What symptoms do you have today?
A fever is a common symptom of the flu.
Call the doctor if your symptoms get worse.
I have no symptoms, but I still feel tired.

ranger.say: a park ranger · a forest ranger
ex: Ask the park ranger where the trail starts.
The ranger told us not to feed the bears.
A forest ranger checks the woods for fires.
Can we talk to a ranger about camping here?
ranger.note: Also a soldier in a special unit: "an Army Ranger." Many sports teams are called "Rangers."

parliament.say: in parliament · a member of parliament
ex: The parliament will vote on the new law next week.
She was elected to parliament last year.
Can we visit the parliament building on Saturday?
How many members does the parliament have?
parliament.note: The US has no parliament; it has "Congress."

ex: Would you like some tomato sauce with that?
This pasta sauce is very easy to make.
Can I have the sauce on the side, please?
This sauce is too spicy for me.

celebrity.say: a TV celebrity · a famous celebrity

object.say: a small object · a metal object
object.note: Also a verb (ob-JECT) meaning "say no to": "I object to this plan."

promotion.say: a special promotion · run a promotion
ex: The store has a special promotion this week.
Is this price part of the summer promotion?
Our new shop needs more promotion online.
The promotion gives you two pizzas for one price.
promotion.note: Most often "promotion" means a better job: "She got a promotion at work."

designer.say: a fashion designer · a web designer

taxi.say: take a taxi · call a taxi · by taxi
taxi.note: In the US, "cab" is also very common.

fort.say: an old fort · in the fort
ex: The old fort is on top of the hill.
Can we visit the fort on Sunday?
Soldiers lived in this fort long ago.
There is a small museum inside the fort.

vampire.say: a vampire movie · believe in vampires
ex: In old stories, vampires only come out at night.
My kids love movies about vampires.
He dressed as a vampire for the costume party.
Do you believe in vampires and ghosts?

pass.say: make a pass · a pass to (a teammate)
ex: He made a long pass to his teammate.
That was a perfect pass from the left side.
She scored a goal after a great pass.
The pass was too short, and they lost the ball.
pass.note: Most often a verb: "pass an exam," "pass the salt." Also a ticket: "a bus pass."

penny.note: In the US, a penny is a one-cent coin. Plural: pennies.

jinn.note: In fairy tales people usually say "genie." Jinn is often also the plural.

argument.say: a good argument · an argument for/against
ex: That's a good argument, but I don't agree.
What is your main argument for this plan?
Her argument against the new rule makes sense.
Give one strong argument for living in a city.
argument.note: Also often a fight with words: "We had an argument."

slide show.say: make a slide show · watch a slide show
ex: I made a slide show of our vacation photos.
Can you play the slide show on the big screen?
Our teacher showed us a slide show about space.
The slide show is ready for the meeting tomorrow.

check.say: the check, please · pay by check
check.note: Most often a verb: "Check your answers." In a US restaurant, the bill is "the check."

avenue.say: on Fifth Avenue · down the avenue
ex: The shop is on Fifth Avenue, near the park.
Turn left onto the avenue at the next light.
We live on a busy avenue downtown.
Excuse me, how do I get to Park Avenue?
avenue.note: In addresses it is often short: Ave.

elephant.say: see an elephant · a baby elephant
ex: We saw three elephants at the zoo today.
The elephant drank water from the river.
An elephant can live for about seventy years.
The baby elephant is walking next to its mother.

outfit.say: a new outfit · wear an outfit
ex: I really love your outfit today!
She bought a new outfit for the party.
What outfit should I wear to the wedding?
This outfit is perfect for a job interview.

tattoo.say: get a tattoo · have a tattoo
ex: He has a tattoo of a dragon on his arm.
She got her first tattoo at eighteen.
My mom doesn't like tattoos at all.
How much does a small tattoo cost here?

opponent.say: beat an opponent · a strong opponent
ex: Our opponent today is a very strong team.
She shook hands with her opponent after the game.
He easily beat his opponent in the final.
Who is your next opponent in the tournament?
The new act protects the rights of workers.
Parliament passed an act on clean water.
This act became law last year.
The new act changes the tax rules for small businesses.
act.note: Most often a verb: "act fast" (do something), "act in a movie."

marketing.say: work in marketing · a marketing team
ex: My sister works in marketing at a big company.
Good marketing helps a small business grow.
Our marketing team has only three people.
I want to study marketing at college.
marketing.note: Uncountable: good marketing, a lot of marketing (not "a marketing").

alliance.say: form an alliance · an alliance with
ex: The two countries formed an alliance last year.
Our company made an alliance with a bigger firm.
The alliance helps protect all its members.
How many countries are in the alliance now?
That's a super idea, let's do it!
This test was super easy for me.
The new teacher is super nice.
Thanks, you were super helpful today!
super.note: Informal. Most often used before an adjective to mean "very": "super easy."

bonus.say: get a bonus · a bonus for

timing.say: good timing · bad timing · perfect timing
ex: Perfect timing, dinner is ready right now!
The timing of the meeting is bad for me.
Good timing is very important in sports.
Bad timing: the store closed five minutes ago.
timing.note: Uncountable: good timing, bad timing (not "a timing").

ex: A helicopter landed on the roof of the hospital.
We flew over the city in a helicopter.
They took the injured man to the hospital by helicopter.
Can you hear that helicopter above our house?

tourist.say: a tourist attraction · popular with tourists

blog.say: write a blog · on my blog · a blog post

block.say: a block of ice · a concrete block
ex: The kids are building a tower with blocks.
Put a block of ice in the cooler.
The wall is made of concrete blocks.
Can you buy a block of cheese for the pizza?
block.note: In the US "block" often means a part of a street: "The shop is two blocks away."

boom.say: a boom in (sales) · a baby boom
ex: There was a housing boom in the city.
The tech boom created many new jobs.
There is a boom in online shopping right now.
The town grew fast during the oil boom.
boom.note: Also a loud sound: "We heard a loud boom."

volunteer.say: work as a volunteer · a volunteer at (a hospital)
ex: She works as a volunteer at the hospital.
We need more volunteers for the school event.
Volunteers cleaned the park on Saturday morning.
Can I sign up as a volunteer here?

comfort.note: Uncountable here (not "a comfort"). Also help when you are sad: "Your words are a comfort."

court.say: a tennis court · on the court
court.note: Most often "court" is a place where a judge decides cases: "go to court."

grant.say: get a grant · apply for a grant
grant.note: Also a verb meaning "give or allow": "The bank granted him a loan."

protest.say: go to a protest · a protest against
ex: There was a big protest in the city today.
Many students went to the protest against the new law.
The protest was peaceful and nobody got hurt.
The road is closed because of a protest.

online.say: buy online · go online · online shopping
ex: I buy most of my clothes online.
Can I pay for the tickets online?
We met online two years ago.
My son has his English lessons online.

jazz.say: listen to jazz · a jazz club
jazz.note: Uncountable: listen to jazz, live jazz (not "a jazz").

bureau.say: a travel bureau · an information bureau

cliff.say: on the cliff · the edge of the cliff

certificate.say: get a certificate · a birth certificate

meter.say: five meters long · ten meters tall
meter.note: Also a machine that measures: "a gas meter," "a parking meter." British spelling: "metre."

camp.say: summer camp · at camp · go to camp
camp.note: Also a place for refugees or prisoners: "a refugee camp." Also a verb: "camp by the lake."

earl.note: A British noble title. "Earl" is also a man's first name in the US.

pub.say: at the pub · go to the pub

passport.say: show your passport · a passport photo
ex: Don't forget to bring your passport to the airport.
My passport expires next month, so I need a new one.
Can I see your passport, please?
She showed her passport at the border.
She is a great athlete and a good student.
The athletes train every morning before school.
He wants to be a professional athlete one day.
Many athletes eat a lot of protein.

chaos.note: Uncountable: total chaos, a lot of chaos (not "a chaos").

ex: Public transport in this city is cheap and fast.
What transport do you use to get to work?
The hotel can help with transport to the airport.
Air transport is faster but more expensive.
transport.note: Uncountable. In the US "transportation" is more common: public transportation.

ex: Her photo got hundreds of likes in one hour.
Thanks for all the likes and comments!
How many likes did your new video get?
He checks his likes every hour on his phone.
like.note: Most often a verb ("I like tea") or "similar to" ("She looks like her mom").

raid.say: a police raid · an air raid · a raid on
ex: Police carried out a raid on the building at dawn.
During the air raid, we stayed in the shelter.
Did you hear the air raid siren last night?
Two soldiers were hurt in the night raid.

menu.say: on the menu · look at the menu
ex: Can I see the menu, please?
The menu has a lot of vegetarian dishes.
What's on the menu for lunch today?
Is there a kids' menu in this cafe?
